label: Weak cosmic censorship (WCC), statement of record
statement_exact: Generically, all singularities in General Relativity arising from regular asymptotically flat initial data should have a complete future null infinity.
assumptions: Einstein field equations (stated for asymptotically flat initial data)
A genericity notion must be supplied separately (topology on the data space); the conjecture as quoted does not fix it
genericity: Left open in the quoted statement; every rigorous positive result below fixes its own topology and its own data class.
topology: Asymptotically flat; future null infinity I+ must be complete.
regularity: Initial data regular; the precise differentiability class is part of what must be fixed per theorem.
scope_caveats: This is an open conjecture, not a theorem.
SRC-011 (Penrose 1969) is metadata-verified only; the wording quoted is from the peer-reviewed 2025 review SRC-001.
does_not_imply: Nothing about strong cosmic censorship.
No statement about non-asymptotically-flat (AdS, compact, or cosmological) settings.
unresolved: Exact original wording in Penrose 1969 not machine-retrieved (paywalled, no arXiv).
No canonical genericity topology agreed in the literature.
falsifiers: Construct a generic family (open set, or positive measure in an explicitly fixed topology) of asymptotically flat initial data satisfying the constraints whose maximal globally hyperbolic development has incomplete future null infinity.
Prove that no such genericity notion can make the conjecture true while keeping the known non-generic naked-singularity examples excluded.
next_action: Bind this statement to the F1 formulation schema once the formulation lead freezes quantifiers.

label: C^0-inextendibility formulation of SCC (attribution disputed)
statement_exact: Strong cosmic censorship in C^0 form: the maximal Cauchy development is inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold with merely continuous metric across its Cauchy horizon.
assumptions: A maximal globally hyperbolic development (MGHD) is fixed.
'Extension' means a non-trivial isometric embedding into a larger C^0 Lorentzian manifold (the embedding may be required to be C^0 or smoother; formulations differ).
Genericity of the initial data must be supplied separately.
genericity: Generic initial data in the class under consideration; the formulation itself does not fix the class.
topology: Depends on the class; for this ledger, asymptotically flat unless stated.
regularity: Metric C^0; no regularity demanded of the connection.
scope_caveats: Attribution split on the accessible primary quotes: THREE independent Dafermos-side sources say 'Christodoulou's C^0 formulation' (Dafermos 2005 CPAM; Dafermos-Rodnianski 2005 Invent. Math.; Dafermos 2003 abstract says 'the strong cosmic censorship conjecture of Roger Penrose'), while Dafermos-Luk 2025 says 'the C^0-inextendibility formulation of Penrose's celebrated ... conjecture' (ambiguous possessive). The name is not settled.

CORRECTED after adversarial review B: an earlier draft said the question 'whether C^0 extensions exist at all' was resolved negatively. That was wrong: C^0 extensions DO exist (Dafermos 2003/2005; Dafermos-Luk 2025). What fails is C^0-inextendibility, i.e. the non-existence of a non-trivial continuous extension.
The 'Penrose 1974 lecture' pointer in the earlier draft was removed: it was not supported by any verified quote.
does_not_imply: Does not demand C^2 or Lipschitz inextendibility.
Does not imply WCC.
unresolved: Which text first stated the C^0 formulation precisely (Penrose 1969/1974 vs Christodoulou 2009 introduction) is unresolved; the origin texts were not retrieved.
Whether the embedding in the definition is required to be C^0 or may be rougher is not uniform across papers.
The attribution count above is over accessible abstract-level quotes only, not a scholarly consensus.
falsifiers: Exhibit a generic family of data whose MGHD admits a non-trivial continuous isometric extension (this is exactly what Dafermos-Luk produce for Kerr-like interior data, conditional on Kerr exterior stability).
Show the formulation is vacuous because every MGHD has a continuous extension.
next_action: Retrieve Penrose's 1974 formulation source and Christodoulou 2009 introduction to close the attribution item.

label: C^2 (and C^k) inextendibility formulation of SCC
statement_exact: Strong cosmic censorship in C^2 form: the maximal globally hyperbolic development is future-inextendible as a Lorentzian manifold whose metric is twice continuously differentiable, for generic initial data.
assumptions: Extension = non-trivial isometric embedding into a larger C^2 Lorentzian manifold.
genericity: Generic data; class-dependent.
regularity: Metric C^2 across the boundary.
scope_caveats: The literature names 'the C^2-formulation' / 'C^2 Strong Cosmic Censorship Conjecture' (Sbierski 2020; Van de Moortel 2020; Luk-Oh-Shlapentokh-Rothman 2022), but the primary text that first isolated the C^2 formulation was not retrieved.
C^2-inextendibility is strictly weaker than C^0-inextendibility: a spacetime can be C^0-extendible but not C^2-extendible.
does_not_imply: Does not imply C^0-inextendibility.
A C^2-inextendibility result in a matter model says nothing directly about vacuum.
unresolved: Primary attribution of the C^2 formulation (Christodoulou 2009 book introduction) not machine-verified; book DOI 10.4171/068 appears only in a secondary bibliography.
Candidate formulation text SRC-092 (Christodoulou 1999 CQG 16 A23-A35) is metadata-only; needs a page check before use.
Whether the intended class is C^2 metrics or C^2 with additional fall-off is not uniform.
falsifiers: Construct generic data whose MGHD admits a C^2 isometric extension across the Cauchy horizon (for the RNdS model with smooth data, Dias-Reall-Santos report exactly this in the linear coupled setting).
Exhibit a C^2-inextendibility proof in the model and show its hypotheses fail on an open set.
next_action: Fetch Christodoulou 2009 introduction (EMS) for the formulation text.

label: 'Christodoulou-Chrusciel version' (continuous metric, L^2 Christoffel symbols)
statement_exact: A version of SCC in which the forbidden extension is one with continuous metric and Christoffel symbols in L^2_loc; failure means the solution can be extended across the Cauchy horizon with continuous metric and square-integrable Christoffel symbols.
assumptions: Extension class = C^0 metric with connection in L^2_loc
genericity: Generic data, class-dependent.
regularity: Metric C^0, Christoffel L^2_loc.
scope_caveats: The name is quoted verbatim from Costa-Girao-Natario-Silva 2018: 'thus violating the Christodoulou-Chrusciel version of strong cosmic censorship'.
The Chrusciel reference intended by that name has not yet been identified in the primary literature; the naming is therefore recorded as a literature usage, not as an established attribution.
does_not_imply: Not the C^2 formulation (L^2 connection is weaker than C^1, hence much weaker than C^2).
Not the C^0 formulation (which forbids even continuous extensions).
unresolved: Identify the Chrusciel paper that defines this version: candidate SRC-090 is now locator-verified (Chrusciel 1992, Contemp. Math. 132, 235-273, DOI 10.1090/conm/132/1188443) but its content is unread, so it cannot yet be cited as scope evidence.
Check whether 'L^2_loc Christoffel' or 'H^1_loc metric' is the intended class.
falsifiers: Locate a primary text defining the Christodoulou-Chrusciel version differently, which would make the quoted usage non-standard and force a rename.
Show that L^2_loc Christoffel extensions exist for generic vacuum data, which would decide the version negatively.
next_action: Search Chrusciel's papers on SCC strength (INSPIRE/arXiv) for the defining statement.

label: Lipschitz / C^{0,1}_loc and L^s_loc-connection formulations (2020-2026)
statement_exact: A family of intermediate inextendibility requirements: the MGHD is not extendible as a Lorentzian manifold in a class where the metric is Lipschitz (C^{0,1}_loc), or where the metric is continuous and the Christoffel symbols lie in L^s_loc for s>1.
assumptions: Extension class fixed by the exponent s or by Lipschitz regularity of the metric
genericity: Class-dependent; Gurriaran 2026 assumes a nonlinear Price-law estimate expected to hold generically.
topology: Asymptotically flat in the quoted results.
regularity: Metric C^{0,1} (Lipschitz), or C^0 with connection in L^s_loc, s>1.
scope_caveats: These formulations are strictly between the C^0 and C^2 formulations in strength.
Results are recent preprints (2020-2026); the 2026 papers are not peer-reviewed in the verified set.
does_not_imply: C^{0,1}_loc-inextendibility does not imply C^2-inextendibility (a C^{0,1} extension could exist even if no C^2 one does).
None of these results settles the C^0 formulation.
unresolved: No uniform definition of 'Lipschitz extension' across the 2026 papers (embedding regularity vs metric regularity).
Publication status of Sbierski 2020 (Duke, per arXiv comment) not machine-confirmed.
falsifiers: Produce a Lipschitz extension of a Kerr Cauchy horizon for generic data, which would falsify the Lipschitz version.
Show the L^s_loc blow-up condition of Cameron-Sbierski 2026 fails on an open set of spherical EM-scalar data.
next_action: Harmonise the exact extension-regularity definitions in the class dossiers once F1/F2 land.

label: [LEAD SYNTHESIS, not a primary theorem] The verdict on SCC/WCC is genericity-class and regularity-class dependent
statement_exact: Across the verified primary literature, changing the topology/regularity class in which initial data are perturbed (smooth vs rough; localized Holder vs BV vs energy space) changes whether naked singularities or Cauchy-horizon extensions are generic, without changing the underlying equations or background solutions.
assumptions: Same background solution family; only the perturbation class/topology changes
genericity: This is a statement about how genericity must be defined, not a theorem about a single class.
regularity: Smooth vs rough (BV, Holder, L^2-based).
scope_caveats: THIS IS A SYNTHESIS BY THE LEAD, not a theorem in any cited paper; it generalizes across independent model problems.
Evidence is assembled from independent model problems (spherical Einstein-scalar; RNdS wave equation), not from one theorem.
The 2026 Zheng preprint is not peer-reviewed.

CORRECTED after adversarial review B: SRC-014 (Christodoulou 1999) was removed as a source; its abstract says nothing about perturbation class or functional framework. It is context for the 1994 family, not evidence for topology-dependence.
does_not_imply: Does not say WCC/SCC are ill-posed; it says scope statements are meaningless without the data topology.
Does not privilege one class as 'the right one'.
unresolved: No consensus canonical topology in the literature.
Quantitative comparison of the topologies used across the cited works has not been done.
falsifiers: Prove that two of the cited perturbation classes induce the same genericity verdict for the same background family and observable, which would weaken the claim to model-dependence.
Find a formulation whose verdict is invariant across all reasonable topologies.
next_action: Feed this into F1/F2 as a hard requirement: every class schema must declare its data-space topology.

label: Christodoulou 1999: instability of spherical scalar-field naked singularities (rough class)
statement_exact: For the spherically symmetric Einstein-massless-scalar-field system, the naked-singularity solutions constructed in 1994 are unstable under sufficiently rough perturbations: within a rough functional framework, perturbations of those data lead to black-hole formation rather than a naked singularity.
assumptions: Massless scalar field coupled to gravity (Einstein-scalar system)
Perturbations measured in a rough functional framework; the precise function space is not fixed by the accessible abstract-level evidence (see unresolved)
This is a statement about the 1994 continuously self-similar naked-singularity family
genericity: The accessible evidence supports 'sufficiently rough perturbations' in 'a rough functional framework'. It does NOT by itself establish a generic-set, open-set, or positive-probability statement.
topology: Spherically symmetric characteristic initial data; asymptotically flat collapse setting.
regularity: Function space not extracted from the primary body; the accessible evidence says 'sufficiently rough perturbations' in a rough functional framework. Review C2 reports that Liu-Li 2018 (SRC-075) restates the result in a BV/codimension framework; that restatement is not independently verified here.
scope_caveats: The arXiv abstract fixes only the system and the question; the precise genericity quantifier is in the paper body, which was not machine-read.

Scope is cross-checked against SRC-046 ('instability to black hole formation under sufficiently rough perturbations ... verifying weak cosmic censorship within a rough functional framework') and SRC-044 ('high co-dimensional nonlinear instability').
Matter is a scalar field, NOT vacuum.
Spherical symmetry is essential to the proof.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC for smooth data, nor for vacuum, nor without symmetry.
Does not say naked singularities cannot form; the 1994 family exists.
Zheng 2026 shows stability of the same family in a localized Holder topology, so this theorem cannot be promoted to 'naked singularities are unstable, period'.
unresolved: Exact theorem number, function space, and quantifier in Christodoulou 1999 not extracted from the paper body (JSTOR/publisher text not machine-accessible; arXiv migration has abstract only).
Whether the statement is about all sufficiently rough perturbations, a dense set, or a codimension statement.
Liu-Li arXiv:1710.02922 (SRC-075) is now locator-verified; its abstract does not state a BV class, so the BV restatement remains unconfirmed.
falsifiers: Construct perturbations of the 1994 data, rough in the same norm, that remain naked-singularity-forming (would contradict the theorem as scoped).
Show the theorem's quantifier is not 'generic' but only 'there exist arbitrarily small rough perturbations', which would force a weaker ledger statement.
next_action: Obtain the 1999 paper body and transcribe the theorem statement verbatim with its norm; then re-promote or keep provisional.

label: Christodoulou 1994: existence of continuously self-similar spherical scalar naked singularities
statement_exact: There exists a one-parameter family of continuously self-similar C^{1,alpha} solutions of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations that form naked singularities.
assumptions: C^{1,alpha} regularity of the solutions (alpha small)
genericity: Non-generic by construction: a one-parameter self-similar family, not an open set in a smooth topology.
topology: Spherically symmetric collapse; naked singularity visible from infinity.
regularity: C^{1,alpha}.
scope_caveats: SRC-013 is metadata-verified only (no abstract available); the precise C^{1,alpha}/self-similar description is quoted from SRC-046 (2026 preprint) and is consistent with SRC-014's framing.
Matter model is a scalar field, not vacuum.
does_not_imply: Does not contradict T-101: existence of a special family is compatible with its instability under rough perturbations.
Does not give an open set of naked-singularity data in any smooth topology.
unresolved: Primary abstract/theorem statement of the 1994 paper not machine-retrieved.
Whether the family is exactly one-parameter with a smooth parameterisation is not confirmed from the primary text.
falsifiers: Find an error in the 1994 construction (no verified claim of this exists in the checked literature).
Show the family fails to be a solution of the Einstein-scalar system (would be a retraction-level event; none found).
next_action: Retrieve Christodoulou 1994 via library access; upgrade or downgrade T-102.

label: Choptuik 1993: critical collapse and the threshold naked singularity
statement_exact: Numerical study of spherically symmetric massless-scalar collapse: a critical parameter value p* separates black-hole-forming from dispersing solutions; the strong-field p->p* limit is universal and generates structure on arbitrarily small spatiotemporal scales, and black-hole masses obey a power law with universal exponent gamma ~ 0.37.
genericity: Threshold behaviour occurs on a codimension-one set (p = p*) in a one-parameter family; it is not claimed generic.
regularity: Numerical smooth data.
scope_caveats: Not a theorem; numerical evidence from 1993.
The threshold solution is the standard heuristic naked singularity; it is not an open-set counterexample to WCC.
SRC-094 (Gundlach-Martin-Garcia, Living Reviews 2007) is a review of the numerical status and states the codimension-one attractor picture.
does_not_imply: Does not prove naked-singularity formation.
Does not establish genericity either way.
unresolved: No rigorous proof of critical-collapse universality located in the verified set; the review confirms the numerical status, not a theorem.
falsifiers: A rigorous computation showing the critical solution is not naked-singular, or that the power law fails outside the tested families.
next_action: Link to Gundlach-Martin-Garcia Living Reviews for the current numerical status (source candidate, unverified).

label: Christodoulou 1984: open set of dust data violates cosmic censorship
statement_exact: For an open subset of initial density distributions of an inhomogeneous spherically symmetric dust cloud, the first singular event (at the centre of symmetry) is the vertex of infinitely many future null geodesic cones that intersect future null infinity; the light rays are infinitely redshifted.
assumptions: Open subset of initial density distributions
Dust energy conditions / standard dust model
genericity: Open set in the stated data family, hence generic in that topology; the model is not vacuum.
regularity: Smooth dust initial data (as used in the paper; exact class not extracted).
scope_caveats: Matter model = dust; this is NOT a vacuum counterexample and must never be cited as one.
Infinitely redshifted rays: visibility from infinity is not the same as a physically observable signal.
does_not_imply: Does not refute AF-WCC-VAC-GEN.
Does not transfer to scalar-field or vacuum models.
unresolved: Exact topology on density distributions in the 1984 paper (C^k? weighted?) not extracted.
falsifiers: Show the singular event is censored in a more careful notion of visibility (e.g. only infinitely redshifted, non-observable radiation), which would demote the counterexample to a weaker 'violation'.
next_action: Compare with shell-crossing literature to fix the visibility convention used in F1.

label: An 2025: anisotropic apparent horizon censors Christodoulou's naked singularity
statement_exact: Employing the Einstein-scalar field system, a tiny anisotropic perturbation from the outgoing characteristic initial data of Christodoulou's naked-singularity solutions leads to an anisotropic apparent horizon that covers and censors the naked singularity; the method proves high co-dimensional nonlinear instability of those solutions.
assumptions: Initial data = Christodoulou's naked-singularity data plus a small anisotropic perturbation on the outgoing characteristic hypersurface
Perturbations allowed finite BV and C^0 norms for shear and scalar derivative; scale-critical norms may be arbitrarily small
genericity: High co-dimensional instability statement; perturbations are small in scale-critical norms but anisotropic.
regularity: Finite BV / C^0 perturbations.
scope_caveats: Published Ann. of Math. 201(3) (2025); DOI 10.4007/annals.2025.201.3.3 now verified via Crossref (SRC-067).
Matter model is Einstein-scalar, NOT vacuum; the AF-WCC-VAC-GEN tag was removed after adversarial review A.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC for generic data: it censors one specific constructed family.
Does not transfer to vacuum without symmetry.
unresolved: Whether the same censoring mechanism works for the non-spherical 2026 construction (SRC-045) is open.
falsifiers: Show the perturbed solution still has a naked singularity visible from infinity (would contradict the theorem as scoped).
Show the anisotropic apparent horizon does not form for the stated perturbation class.
next_action: Cross-link to F1's AF-WCC-SCALAR-SPH schema (same matter model, no symmetry in perturbation).

label: An-Wu 2026: non-spherical Einstein-scalar naked singularities with singular inner Cauchy horizon
statement_exact: There exist non-spherically-symmetric solutions of the 3+1-dimensional Einstein-scalar field system with incomplete future null infinity and a singular inner Cauchy horizon, obtained by prescribing non-spherical data along incoming and outgoing null hypersurfaces; the solutions satisfy C^{1,kappa/(1-kappa)+} inextendibility at the inner Cauchy horizon for self-similar parameter kappa in (0,1/3).
assumptions: Characteristic initial data on two transversely intersecting null hypersurfaces
No symmetry assumed; constructed from a generalisation of Christodoulou's self-similar solution
genericity: Constructed family; not claimed generic.
topology: 3+1, characteristic problem; incomplete I+ in the constructed solutions.
regularity: C^{1,kappa/(1-kappa)+} inextendibility of the inner horizon.
scope_caveats: Preprint (v1, July 2026, 116 pages); not peer-reviewed.
Matter model is a scalar field, not vacuum.
Failure of WCC here is 'in its strict formulation' for constructed, non-generic data.
does_not_imply: Does not refute generic WCC.
Does not give a vacuum naked singularity.
unresolved: Refereeing status.
Whether the construction has an open neighbourhood of data with the same behaviour.
falsifiers: Find a gap in the global existence/inextendibility proof (preprint, unreviewed).
Show the constructed spacetimes are C^{1,...}-extendible across the inner horizon.
next_action: Re-check arXiv version and any journal reference at next checkpoint; if unchanged, keep provisional.

label: Zheng 2026: nonlinear stability of the self-similar naked singularities in a Holder topology
statement_exact: A one-parameter family of continuously self-similar C^{1,alpha} naked-singularity solutions of the spherically symmetric Einstein-scalar field equations is nonlinearly stable under initial perturbations lying in a small open neighbourhood of the generating data, measured in a localized Holder topology, with perturbations of the same regularity as the background.
assumptions: Perturbations in a localized Holder topology, same regularity as the background (C^{1,alpha})
Relies on a companion linearized-stability paper (Singh-Zheng) not yet verified
genericity: Open neighbourhood of naked-singularity data IN THE HOLDER TOPOLOGY; the complement statement holds in the rough topology of T-101.
topology: Localized Holder topology on initial data.
regularity: C^{1,alpha}.
scope_caveats: Preprint (v1, May 2026); not peer-reviewed.
Part I of a series; the companion linearized stability result is cited but not independently verified here.
Does not contradict T-101: different topology, so both can hold.
does_not_imply: Does not make naked singularities generic in a smooth/rough topology.
Does not establish WCC or its failure for the class as a whole.
unresolved: The companion paper (Singh-Zheng, Part II) not yet fetched/verified.
Whether the Holder topology is physically/numerically natural is a modelling judgement, not settled by the preprint.
falsifiers: Find an error in the nonlinear stability proof (preprint).
Show the localized Holder topology is empty/trivial for the constraint equations, which would make the open neighbourhood vacuous.
next_action: Verify the companion Singh-Zheng linearized stability paper and the exact topology definition.

label: Christodoulou 2009: trapped-surface formation from short-pulse vacuum data
statement_exact: For the Einstein vacuum equations in 3+1 dimensions with no symmetry assumptions, there is an open set of regular initial conditions on an outgoing null hypersurface, of short-pulse type, whose future development forms a trapped surface; the theorems are the first long-time dynamics result for data not confined to a small neighbourhood of Minkowski data.
assumptions: Characteristic initial data on an outgoing null hypersurface plus incoming Minkowski data
genericity: Open set within the short-pulse family (as restated by SRC-042: 'an open set of regular initial conditions'); NOT an open set of general asymptotically flat data.
topology: Characteristic initial value problem; asymptotically flat.
regularity: Regular data (specific differentiability fixed in the monograph).
scope_caveats: SRC-041 is the MG12 conference chapter (2012, pp. 24-34); the EMS Monograph is SRC-054 (arXiv:0805.3880) with DOI 10.4171/068 verified via Crossref.
Short-pulse data are special, not generic in the space of all AF data.
Trapped-surface formation is not by itself complete future null infinity (WCC), though it is the standard precursor.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC for generic AF vacuum data.
Does not construct a black-hole exterior with complete I+.
unresolved: Precise statement and constants of the main theorem not extracted from the book.
Relation between 'trapped surface forms' and 'I+ is complete' needs the standard global argument, not contained in this theorem.
falsifiers: Find an error in the short-pulse mechanism (no retraction found in the verified set).
Show the trapped surface forms but the solution still has incomplete I+ (would decouple the two notions and change the WCC evidence map).
next_action: Link this entry to the AF-WCC-VAC-BH-FORM support class and to the DHRT near-Schwarzschild result.

label: Klainerman-Rodnianski 2012: simpler trapped-surface formation, enlarged data set
statement_exact: A simpler proof of finite trapped-surface formation in vacuum, enlarging the admissible set of initial conditions of Christodoulou's short-pulse result and relaxing the propagation estimates, while reducing the number of derivatives of the curvature needed from two to one.
assumptions: Characteristic initial data; finite problem (initial outgoing null hypersurface)
genericity: Enlarged open admissible set relative to Christodoulou's, still a special short-pulse class.
regularity: One derivative of curvature (weaker than Christodoulou's two).
scope_caveats: Confirms that T-201's data class is open but special.
Finite problem, not the full past-null-infinity version.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC.
unresolved: Exact definition of the enlarged class not extracted.
falsifiers: Locate an error in the relaxed estimates (no retraction found).
Show the enlarged class fails to contain Christodoulou's, which would contradict the stated comparison.

label: Li-Yu 2015: complete AF vacuum Cauchy data free of trapped surfaces evolving to a trapped surface
statement_exact: There exists complete, asymptotically flat vacuum Cauchy initial data, free of trapped surfaces, whose future development must admit a trapped surface; the data equal a constant-time Minkowski slice inside and a constant-time Kerr slice outside.
assumptions: Gluing construction using Christodoulou's black-hole formation theorem and Corvino-Schoen gluing
genericity: Existence of a special family; not generic.
regularity: Smooth (gluing class; exact differentiability in the paper).
scope_caveats: arXiv ID 1207.3164 now directly verified (primary page fetch); the DOI 10.4007/annals.2015.181.2.6 and Annals volume 181(2) 699-768 remain secondary-anchored.
Trapped-surface formation only; no claim about exterior completeness or about I+.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC for generic data.
Does not construct a naked singularity.
unresolved: Verify DOI 10.4007/annals.2015.181.2.6 via Crossref.
Exact differentiability/decay of the glued data not extracted.
falsifiers: Find a gap in the gluing argument (no retraction found).
Show the resulting development fails to be asymptotically flat, which would break the AF class binding.
next_action: L1: confirm arXiv:1207.3167 and DOI 10.4007/annals.2015.181.2.6 via arXiv/Crossref.

label: DHRT 2021: nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild with complete future null infinity
statement_exact: General vacuum initial data with no symmetry, sufficiently close to Schwarzschild data and constrained to a teleologically constructed codimension-3 submanifold of moduli space, evolve to a vacuum spacetime that (i) possesses a complete future null infinity I+ whose past is bounded by a regular future-complete event horizon, (ii) remains close to Schwarzschild in the exterior, and (iii) asymptotes back to a member of the Schwarzschild family.
assumptions: Initial data sufficiently close to Schwarzschild
Data constrained to a codimension-3 submanifold of moduli space (teleologically constructed)
genericity: Open neighbourhood of Schwarzschild data intersected with a codimension-3 submanifold; not generic among all AF data, but an open set in a natural restricted class.
topology: Asymptotically flat, exterior region of a black hole.
regularity: Smooth data in the relevant topology (double-null gauges).
scope_caveats: Preprint (513 pages, 2021); no journal reference on arXiv as of 2026-09-11.
Clause (i) is a rigorous positive WCC-type statement only for near-Schwarzschild data.
The codimension-3 restriction means the result does not cover generic perturbations.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC for generic AF vacuum data.
Does not say anything about the black-hole interior beyond the event horizon (no SCC content).
unresolved: Peer-review status.
Whether the codimension-3 restriction can be removed or replaced by the Kerr family.
falsifiers: Find an error in the 513-page preprint (no retraction found).
Show the submanifold restriction is empty, making the theorem vacuous.
next_action: Track journal status; if published, upgrade citation; re-check for a 2025-2026 journal version.

label: Klainerman-Szeftel 2020: nonlinear stability of Schwarzschild under polarized perturbations
statement_exact: Nonlinear stability of the Schwarzschild spacetime under axially symmetric polarized perturbations: solutions of the Einstein vacuum equations for asymptotically flat 1+3-dimensional Lorentzian metrics admitting a hypersurface-orthogonal spacelike Killing field with closed orbits.
assumptions: Axisymmetric polarized perturbations (hypersurface-orthogonal spacelike Killing field with closed orbits)
genericity: Restricted symmetry class; not generic AF data.
regularity: Smooth.
scope_caveats: Book metadata verified: Annals of Mathematics Studies 210, Princeton University Press (2020), ISBN 9780691212425, DOI 10.23943/princeton/9780691212425.001.0001 (SRC-038); the abstract claim that the restriction is largely to ensure a Schwarzschild final state is from the source.
The polarized class is symmetry-restricted, not an open set of general AF data.
does_not_imply: Does not prove WCC for general vacuum data.
Does not cover rotating final states.
unresolved: Determine how much of the polarized-class argument is needed beyond symmetry (the source says the restriction is largely to force a Schwarzschild final state).
falsifiers: Find an error in the proof (no retraction found).
Show the polarized class does not contain a neighbourhood of Schwarzschild within its symmetry class, contradicting stability.
next_action: L1: verify arXiv ID/DOI via arXiv API and Crossref before upgrading.

label: GKS 2022: nonlinear stability of slowly rotating Kerr
statement_exact: The nonlinear stability of the Kerr family for small angular momentum (|a|/m << 1) is proved; the paper completes the proof of the Main Theorem of the GKS programme by supplying the nonlinear wave estimates.
assumptions: Small perturbations of Kerr data (as set up in the GKS series)
genericity: Open neighbourhood of slowly rotating Kerr data; not generic AF data and not the full subextremal range.
regularity: Smooth.
scope_caveats: Preprint (2022); no journal reference on arXiv as of 2026-09-11.
Small angular momentum only; the full subextremal nonlinear range is NOT covered (only linear stability is, SRC-063). See T-515 for the verified status table.
This is the key input needed to discharge the antecedent in T-301 (Dafermos-Luk), and it only covers |a|/m << 1.
does_not_imply: Does not automatically prove the C^0 SCC failure for all subextremal Kerr; that requires the Dafermos-Luk conditional plus this stability result plus retrieval of the interior data assumptions.
unresolved: Publication status.
Exact statement of the Main Theorem (Section 3.4 of the GKS book) not extracted.
Full-subextremal nonlinear stability: now CLAIMED by Hintz 2026 (SRC-078, T-528/SRC-078); this small-|a|/m result remains the peer-review-track antecedent.
falsifiers: Find an error in the GKS series (no retraction found).

label: Rodnianski-Shlapentokh-Rothman 2023: vacuum naked-singularity exterior solution
statement_exact: There exist solutions of the 3+1-dimensional Einstein vacuum equations corresponding to the exterior region of a naked singularity, constructed via a new type of self-similarity and a geometric twisting phenomenon.
assumptions: The construction gives the exterior region; the full maximal development requires gluing to an interior solution
genericity: Constructed self-similar family; not generic.
topology: 3+1 vacuum; naked singularity visible from infinity in the constructed exterior.
regularity: Smooth in the constructed region (specific regularity in the paper).
scope_caveats: Published Ann. of Math. 198(1) 231-391 (2023); now confirmed by a direct Crossref record (SRC-068), closing the earlier metadata gap.
Exterior solution alone is not a complete counterexample to WCC: one must glue to the interior (SRC-003, preprint) and verify the resulting maximal development.
The abstract itself says the only previous naked singularities were Christodoulou's scalar-field ones (plus numerical/higher-dimensional), and this work 'initiates' the vacuum study.
does_not_imply: Does not refute generic WCC (the data are special/self-similar).
Does not establish that the glued object is the MGHD of smooth AF data until SRC-003 is verified.
unresolved: Journal reference for SRC-002 not machine-verified on the primary page (L1 gap).
SRC-003 (interior) is an unpublished 2022 preprint; gluing theorem not peer-reviewed.
Whether the exterior data arise from an open set of AF initial data is not claimed.
falsifiers: Find an error in the self-similar construction.
Show the exterior cannot be glued to any interior solution satisfying the vacuum equations, which would invalidate the naked-singularity interpretation.
